correctness.rationale: For ordinary crown-graph forcing, three whites on one side can never be decreased, so every forcing set has at most two white vertices per bipartition side. Four-white configurations force exactly when the two omitted index-pairs differ, by explicit forces. This gives the diagonal-deleted Cartesian square of J(n,2). Any Johnson geodesic can avoid one forbidden third vertex, and explicit three-/four-step routes handle swaps; the exceptional adjacent swap has a sharp two-step obstruction. Inclusion-exclusion over both diagonal conditions and the exact Nk adjacent swaps gives the full distance enumerator, diameter and Wiener index for every n≥3. Two independent exhaustive finite programs checking forcing closure and Johnson-pair BFS at n=3..8 passed; no finite-to-infinite extrapolation is used.

originality.rationale: The compared earlier exact forcing polynomial for complete bipartite graphs with a matching deleted already covers the minimum crown forcing configurations and their count. Those are explicitly excluded from novelty. The new claim is the complete source-target shortest-path metric with its unique adjacent-swap penalty and all-pairs distance polynomial, not logically supplied merely by the previous counting polynomial or the general definition of a reconfiguration graph. The inspected full-text 2020 reconfiguration paper poses shortest distance calculation as an open methodological question but has no crown/Johnson-square theorem. Relevant targeted literature and published research-record queries identified no covering metric theorem. Unindexed equivalent metric results remain a risk.
residual_risks: Earlier broad forcing-set work already settles all configuration counts and must not be interpreted as new.
Equivalent graph-distance formulas may have appeared in a nonindexed Johnson-graph or two-particle configuration-space source.
The complete text of every conceivable historical article was not accessible; no claim of uniqueness or independent external validation is made.

value.rationale: The exact shortest-path formula, with precisely one exceptional swap obstruction, determines all source-target reconfiguration costs in an infinite natural family. The complete distance enumerator and Wiener index provide metric distribution information, not just reachability or known state counts. The 2020 foundational reconfiguration paper explicitly raises efficient shortest-path computation as a research direction; this gives a complete closed-form answer on matching-deleted complete bipartite crown graphs. These are motivated and nontrivial despite the known forcing-set classification.
